items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: a wonderful arranger by a name of Don Redman

ctx.x: was led by Don Redman and they came to work for a short time, possibly, oh, six weeks or so at Sebastian's Cotton Club in Culver City (PHONETIC), which was the biggest nightclub in the world. It seated something like 1750 people for dinner with three dance floors in it.

I was working with Curtis Moseby at the time up in San Francisco at the Apex Number Two. So, when McKinney's Cotton Pickers came out, they had four saxaphones in the band and in the early days when you had three saxaphones, that's a whole lot of saxaphones. So, these guys came out and had four saxaphones in the band and a wonderful arranger by a name of Don Redman. He had those saxaphones sounding so good that Les Hite's band, who was the house band there and followed them back in when they left, they had to try…

So, they called the kid up in San Francisco, who was me, and I came down and joined them. That's when I started working again with Lawrence. He was in that band at the time. He had left the number two band of Curtis Moseby up in San Francisco and had come to work with Les Hite at the time, so we started another allegiance and alliance with each other.
